name: Cor triatriatum sinister
aliases: Cor triatriatum of the left atrium

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and imaging diagnostic criteria for cor triatriatum sinister

criteria.description: Presence of a fibromuscular membrane dividing the left atrium into two distinct chambers
Pulmonary veins draining into the proximal (posterior-superior) chamber
Communication between the proximal and distal left atrial chambers through one or more fenestrations in the membrane
Doppler evidence of flow gradient across the membrane indicating obstruction
Symptoms consistent with left atrial obstruction such as dyspnea or pulmonary hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a fibromuscular membrane dividing the left atrium with pulmonary venous drainage into the proximal chamber and communication between chambers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities, especially echocardiography and cardiac MRI or CT.

laboratory: Nonspecific findings; possible elevated BNP in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing fibromuscular membrane in left atrium
Doppler demonstrating flow gradient across membrane
Cardiac MRI or CT confirming anatomy and pulmonary venous drainage
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Cardiac catheterization may show pressure gradient between proximal and distal left atrial chambers

distinguishingFeatures: Valve leaflet thickening and restricted motion rather than intra-atrial membrane
Characteristic mitral valve gradient on echocardiography
Pulmonary veins drain anomalously outside left atrium
